runs.text: THE CORE IDEA

transcript.sourceText: THE CORE IDEA
transcript.text: THE CORE IDEA

runs.text: A monopoly has durable market power because barriers prevent close rivals from entering and eroding that power. Barriers can keep profit from triggering the entry response that erodes profit in competitive markets. Natural monopoly can make one-firm production cost-efficient while still creating a market-power problem.

runs.text: Across the relevant output range, the graph's ATC curve declines as output expands, so one large producer can supply the market at lower average cost than several small firms. Time: 5 minutes
Outcome: Identify Monopoly Power, Barriers to Entry & Sources of Monopoly.
Difficulty: Intermediate
THE CORE IDEA

A monopoly has durable market power because barriers prevent close rivals from entering and eroding that power. Barriers can keep profit from triggering the entry response that erodes profit in competitive markets. Natural monopoly can make one-firm production cost-efficient while still creating a market-power problem.
HOW TO RECOGNIZE IT
A city has one coffee shop today, but entry is easy and several rivals are preparing to open.
A software firm is the only seller this year.
The current one-seller market does not by itself establish durable monopoly power.
One seller becomes a durable monopoly only when entry is meaningfully blocked.
WATCH OUT

Do not treat any large firm as monopoly. Durable monopoly power depends on the relevant market and barriers to entry. A monopoly requires meaningful barriers to entry, not merely one seller at a moment in time.
WORKED EXAMPLE: IDENTIFYING MONOPOLY POWER

Across the relevant output range, the graph's ATC curve declines as output expands, so one large producer can supply the market at lower average cost than several small firms. That cost structure supports natural monopoly. At the efficient point where demand meets MC, price would be below ATC, creating a regulatory funding problem.
